answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, with rewards released only after independent peers verify useful work. If one operator spins up a falcon fleet of fake accounts, each must still lock capital, and detected fraud forfeits that stake; splitting identities does not dilute the total cost. A nebula of sybils therefore cannot cheaply dominate votes or harvest rewards, while honest newcomers can build reputation gradually. The attacker pays an opportunity cost for every identity and risks losing the stake at nadir.
